hook.text: Flip a coin 1,000 times: roughly 50-50. Flip it 10 times: anything can happen. Small populations work the same way.

buildup.text: Genetic drift is random change in allele frequency. In small groups, luck determines which genes survive—not fitness.

discovery.text: Kimura's neutral theory showed most evolutionary changes are from drift, not selection.

twist.text: Drift can eliminate beneficial alleles and fix harmful ones.

climax.text: In large populations, selection rules. In small ones, drift rules. Population size decides which force wins.

punchline.text: Evolution isn't always survival of the fittest.

quiz.question: According to neutral theory, what drives most molecular evolution?
